46	2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.
47	3. **FIXED (commit e02e62d, migration `20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql`)**: `checkout_transaction` only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduced inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all. Fixed by decoupling the Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (posted only when `v_total > 0`) from the HPP/Persediaan lines (posted independently whenever `v_total_cost > 0`), building `v_journal_lines` incrementally and only calling `private.post_journal` if at least 2 lines ended up in it. Mirrored the identical fix in `void_transaction`'s reversing entry. Verified end-to-end in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Roti Bakar (HPP Rp5.300) with a 100% order discount (INV-20260709-0001, total Rp0) — jurnal correctly posted a 2-line entry (debit 5-001 HPP / credit 1-200 Persediaan, Rp5.300, no Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines). Then voided it with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly posted debit 1-200 / credit 5-001, Rp5.300. Neraca stayed balanced throughout.
48	4. **FIXED (commit 23c83ca)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` called the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }`. Verified no regression on the happy path (a normal "Lain-lain" expense still saved silently with no error banner). The failure path itself wasn't exercised (would need deliberately breaking an account code) but the logic is a straightforward null-check/ternary, low risk.
49	
50	**All 4 formula-audit bugs are now fixed** (commits bdbe337, b928d51, e02e62d, 23c83ca). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

52	**5th bug found and fixed 2026-07-10** (user asked "sebagai accounting & finance saran apa yg kurang" — a fresh accounting-lens review after the mini-ERP feature set was otherwise complete): `checkout_transaction` credited the **full transaction total — including PPN collected from the customer — straight to 4-001 Pendapatan Penjualan**. PPN isn't the business's revenue, it's a liability held on behalf of the tax office, so every taxed sale was overstating income with no corresponding "PPN payable" anywhere in Kewajiban. **Fixed migration `20260710140000_ppn_liability.sql`**: added `2-200 PPN Keluaran (Utang Pajak)` to the seeded COA (via `seed_default_accounts` + backfill for existing businesses), and redefined `checkout_transaction` to credit only `subtotal + service` to Pendapatan Penjualan while crediting `tax` to the new liability account instead (Kas & Bank debit for the full total is unchanged). `void_transaction`'s reversing entry mirrors the same split. Remitting the PPN later (paying the tax office) needs no new UI — the existing Jurnal Manual page already lists every account dynamically, so it's just a manual debit-2-200/credit-1-001 entry. Historical transactions posted before this fix keep their PPN baked into revenue (not retroactively corrected — would need a manual correcting entry if that matters).
53	- Verified E2E in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Kopi Susu (Rp18.000 + 5% layanan Rp900 + 10% PPN Rp1.890 = Rp20.790 total, tax_enabled/service_enabled both on for this business) → journal posted debit Kas & Bank 20.790 / credit Pendapatan Penjualan **18.900** (not 20.790) / credit PPN Keluaran **1.890**, plus the usual HPP/Persediaan lines, balanced (27.790 = 27.790 incl. HPP). Neraca showed PPN Keluaran Rp1.890 under Kewajiban and Laba Berjalan correctly reflecting only the Rp11.900 margin (18.900 revenue − 7.000 HPP), still balanced. Then voided the same transaction with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly flipped debit/credit on all three split lines (debit Pendapatan 18.900, debit PPN Keluaran 1.890, credit Kas & Bank 20.790, plus HPP/Persediaan reversal), balanced.

No migration needed — reads existing tables only.
57	- Verified in browser: right after the Tutup Buku test above, selecting "Semua" period showed **Rp0 everywhere** — correct, not a bug, since the closing entry (dated today, same as all the test activity) nets every pendapatan/beban account back to zero within any period range that includes it, exactly like a real closed period would. Sold 1 Roti Bakar afterward (new activity postdating the closing calc) — the report then correctly showed Pendapatan Penjualan Rp17.325 (subtotal+service only, no PPN — confirms the PPN fix above flows through here too), HPP Rp5.300, Laba Kotor Rp12.025, Laba Bersih Rp12.025, margin 69%, and this number matched Neraca's "Laba Berjalan (belum ditutup)" (also Rp12.025) exactly, confirming the two reports stay consistent with each other.

Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": created a payslip for Manajer Test (Rp0 base pay, no attendance), added a Rp150.000 "Bonus Test" tunjangan, marked paid → Jurnal correctly showed debit Beban Gaji / credit Kas & Bank Rp150.000, Neraca stayed balanced. 60	- Payroll's accounting picture is now complete: sales, expenses, purchases, and payroll all auto-post; only Akuntansi's own manual-entry pages don't need auto-posting since they *are* the manual path.
61	
62	**THR/Lembur first-class fields — built and verified E2E 2026-07-10**: closes the last gap noted above. User chose manual-nominal-only for both (no jam×tarif breakdown for lembur, no proportional-tenure formula for THR — both vary too much per business to hardcode). Migration `20260710110000_payslip_thr_lembur.sql` adds `payslips.lembur_amount`/`thr_amount numeric not null default 0`. New action `updatePayslipExtras` (payroll/actions.ts) updates both at once, guarded by the same `paid_at` lock as adjustments. Both the payslip detail breakdown and the payroll list's total now fold `lembur_amount + thr_amount` into `totalDiterima`/`total`, and `markPayslipPaid`'s journal-posting total includes them too. 63	
64	**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). Deliberately additive/separate from the existing `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` "Pembelian Bahan Baku/Barang Dagang" categories — this is a new, more structured flow for supplier-attributed purchases that can be paid partially or fully on credit, not a replacement.
65	- New pages: `suppliers/page.tsx` (CRUD list + outstanding-utang badge computed from purchases) and `purchases/page.tsx` (record a purchase — mirrors `add-expense-form.tsx`'s ingredient/product conditional UI and weighted-average cost recalc exactly, plus a 3-way payment-mode picker: Lunas Sekarang / Bayar Sebagian / Semua Utang — with inline "+ Bayar" installment forms per unpaid purchase row).
66	- `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase` posts a journal entry via the same `post_journal_entry` RPC pattern as `finance/actions.ts` (debit 1-200 Persediaan for the full amount; credit 1-001 Kas & Bank for whatever's paid now, credit 2-001 Utang Dagang for the remainder — 2 or 3 lines depending on payment mode). `addPurchasePayment` posts debit 2-001 / credit 1-001 for each installment and rejects overpayment past the remaining balance. Ingredient purchases also insert into `ingredient_price_history` (source `'pembelian'`) same as the expense flow, see [[mini-erp-scope]]'s Tren Harga section above.
67	- Nav: "🧾 Pembelian & Hutang" and "🏬 Supplier" added to the Operasional sidebar group (not fnb-gated — retail businesses get both too, just without the ingredient option; tiket excluded like the rest of Operasional's inventory items).
68	- Verified in browser: added supplier "CV Sumber Rejeki", bought 500gr Gula Pasir for Rp15.000 fully on credit → journal posted debit Persediaan/credit Utang Dagang Rp15.000 correctly (2-line entry, no Kas & Bank line since paid_amount=0), stock updated 1000→1500gr. Paid Rp10.000 installment → journal posted debit Utang Dagang/credit Kas & Bank Rp10.000, purchase row updated to "Sisa Rp5.000", supplier badge showed "Utang Rp5.000", Neraca stayed balanced throughout (Aset = Kewajiban + Modal confirmed after each step).
69	- UI quirk hit during testing, useful for future preview-tool sessions on this project: clicking a `useActionState`-wired submit button (`<form action={formAction}>`, a React-specific mechanism) immediately after `window.location.href` navigation can silently no-op if it fires before hydration completes — no network request, no error, just nothing happens. Re-clicking (or waiting a beat) after confirming the click actually landed fixes it. This is distinct from the earlier-documented plain-`onClick`-button pattern (edit-ingredient-form.tsx-style inline forms), which doesn't have this hydration race since... actually both need hydration; the symptom just presents differently (edit forms fail to open at all if unhydrated, vs. server-action forms open fine but silently eat the submit).
70	
71	**Tren Harga bahan baku — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: new `public.ingredient_price_history` table (migration `20260709100000_ingredient_price_history.sql`, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) is an append-only log (`business_id`, `ingredient_id`, `unit_cost`, `source` in `awal`/`pembelian`/`manual`, `created_at`), backfilled with each existing ingredient's current price as an `awal` row. Two write sites: `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` inserts a `pembelian` row when a "Pembelian Bahan Baku" expense changes the weighted-average `unit_cost`; `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient` inserts a `manual` row when the manual-edit form changes `unit_cost` (compares against the pre-update value fetched first). New page `reports/price-trend/page.tsx` — period filter (30/90 hari/semua), naik/turun-harga summary counts, and a `<details>`-per-ingredient list (server-component-friendly, no client JS) showing current vs baseline price and full history on expand. Nav link "🏷️ Tren Harga" added next to "Bahan Baku" in the Operasional sidebar group (fnb-only, same gate as Bahan Baku itself). Verified in browser: bought Gula Pasir at a higher price → showed up as `pembelian` entry and flagged "Naik Harga: 1 bahan"; edited its price manually via the ingredients page's inline edit (a client-state form with no `<form>` tag — Simpan is a plain button, so driving it via preview tools requires the native-setter + dispatchEvent('input') trick, not `preview_fill`, to get React's onChange to fire) → showed up as a third `manual` entry, history list correctly ordered newest-first (Edit manual Rp25 → Pembelian Rp21 → Awal Rp18).
72	
73	**Akuntansi module — built 2026-07-08** (user explicitly chose auto-posting from transactions, and all 4 reports at once, overriding the "doesn't need to be complete" framing for this specific piece):
74	- Schema: `public.accounts` (Chart of Accounts, seeded per-business via trigger + backfill with a standard Indonesian F&B/retail COA — Kas & Bank, Persediaan, Utang Dagang, Modal Pemilik, Pendapatan Penjualan, Beban Pokok Penjualan, Beban Gaji/Sewa/Listrik/Marketing/Perlengkapan/Lain-lain), `public.journal_entries` + `public.journal_lines` (double-entry, journal tables are SELECT-only from the client — all writes go through `private.post_journal()` so an unbalanced entry can never be persisted), `public.budgets` (Target vs Aktual). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the 3 pending migration files.
75	- Auto-posting wired into `checkout_transaction` (sales → debit Kas/Bank + credit Pendapatan, plus debit HPP/credit Persediaan when the sale has recipe cost data) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). Expense recording (`finance/actions.ts` → `addExpense`) also auto-posts via the new `post_journal_entry` RPC — purchases hit Persediaan, other categories map to a fixed category→account table (`EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` in that file).
76	- Payroll does NOT auto-post yet — payslip actions still write directly to tables with no RPC, deliberately deferred rather than expanding this delivery further. If asked to close this gap, same pattern as the expense hook applies.
77	- 5 new pages under `/business/<id>/accounting/`: `daftar-akun` (CRUD custom accounts, system accounts can't be deleted), `jurnal` (period-filtered list + manual multi-line entry form with live debit=credit balance check), `neraca` (balance sheet as-of a date, with an unclosed "Laba Berjalan" line in Modal since there's no formal period-closing process — if aset≠kewajiban+modal it flags a visible warning), `arus-kas` (cash flow from the Kas & Bank account only, bucketed into Operasional vs "Investasi & Pendanaan (manual)"), `anggaran` (monthly budget per pendapatan/beban account vs actual from the journal). All wired into a new "Akuntansi" sidebar group in `dashboard-shell.tsx` (hidden for `tiket` business type, same as the existing Keuangan/Laporan group).

User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).

**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. Shows revenue/COGS/margin per category and per product, flags products with no HPP data (cost=0) and products under 20% margin.
- **Tren Harga bahan baku** — still missing, needs a new price-history table (`ingredients.unit_cost` only stores the current value, no history). Not started.
- Full double-entry **Akuntansi module** (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual) — still entirely missing, and is a much bigger lift (new schema for accounts + journal lines, plus a decision on how it relates to the existing cash-basis Laba Rugi/Keuangan pages — replace or coexist?). Not started; user chose to do Cost Control/HPP first, accounting module "menyusul" (comes after).
- **Operasional gaps** not yet addressed: formal Pembelian (purchasing) records beyond the existing `expenses` category tagging, Supplier & Hutang (accounts payable) tracking — no supplier table exists yet.

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. As of 2026-07-09 every item originally identified in this gap analysis has been built and verified E2E — no queued next candidate remains; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.

**Post-gap-analysis follow-ups identified 2026-07-10** (user asked "apa yg kurang" after the original list was exhausted): two remaining holes found by re-auditing against the reference — (1) Piutang Usaha (AR) had a COA account but no feature writing to it — **closed same day**, see below. (2) No formal tutup buku (period-closing) process — **closed same day**, see below. As of 2026-07-10, no further gaps are queued against the original reference; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.

**Second accounting-lens follow-up round, same day**: after #1 (PPN) and #2 (accrual Laba Rugi) above, user said "lanjut semua" for the remaining 4 suggestions — all built and verified same session:
- **Fixed asset depreciation** — new `fixed_assets` + `depreciation_postings` tables (migration `20260710150000_fixed_assets_depreciation.sql`), new `1-501 Akumulasi Penyusutan` account (aset-type but `normal_balance='debit'` deliberately, even though only ever credited — see the migration's own comment for why this correctly reduces Total Aset in Neraca's generic per-account summing without special-casing). New page `assets/page.tsx` ("🖥️ Aset Tetap" in Operasional): capitalize a purchase (debit 1-500/credit 1-001), then a confirm-gated "Posting Penyusutan Bulan Ini" button computing straight-line depreciation `(cost−salvage)/useful_life_months` across all active assets and posting one aggregate entry (debit 5-105 Beban Penyusutan/credit 1-501), guarded against double-posting the same month via a `unique(business_id, period)` constraint.
  - **Bug hit and fixed during verification**: the eligibility filter used `purchase_date <= period` (period = first-of-month) which wrongly excluded assets bought mid-month (e.g. bought the 10th, period="...-01" → excluded). Fixed to compare against the *last* day of the period's month instead.
  - **Second bug hit and fixed**: `depreciation_postings` migration only granted a SELECT RLS policy (wrongly assuming writes would go through a security-definer RPC like `close_accounting_period`), but the actual write is a direct client insert from the Next.js action (same pattern as `fixed_assets`) — INSERT was rejected by RLS. Fixed via a follow-up migration `20260710160000_fix_depreciation_postings_rls.sql` granting `for all using/with check owns_business`, matching `fixed_assets`'s policy.
  - **Data cleanup consequence, real and worth remembering**: the first bug fix required a page reload + retry, but the *second* (RLS) failure happened **after** the journal-posting RPC call had already succeeded (post_journal_entry is security-definer, unaffected by the depreciation_postings RLS gap) — so the failed attempt still posted a real "Beban Penyusutan 2026-07" journal entry before erroring out on the tracking-table insert. The next successful retry posted a *second* identical entry, leaving Akumulasi Penyusutan double-counted (Rp200.000 instead of Rp100.000) even though `fixed_assets.accumulated_depreciation` and `depreciation_postings` only reflected one. Caught by comparing the Aset Tetap page's book value against Neraca's Akumulasi Penyusutan line — they should always match and didn't. Fixed via a manual reversing journal entry (debit 1-501/credit 5-105, Rp100.000) through the Jurnal Manual page, per the app's established "correct via reversing entry, don't edit old rows" convention — not by deleting the duplicate journal_entries row. **Lesson for any future multi-step server action that calls a security-definer RPC before a plain-RLS insert**: if the plain insert can fail independently, the RPC's effect is not transactional with it and can leave an orphaned side-effect: sanity-check derived totals (e.g. a book-value calc) against the source-of-truth ledger (Neraca) after any action that touches both, not just after known-risky ones.
- **AR/AP aging** — no schema change; added a 4-bucket (0-30/31-60/61-90/90+ hari) breakdown directly to the existing `receivables/page.tsx` and `purchases/page.tsx` (only rendered when there's an outstanding balance), bucketing each unpaid row by `today − date`.
- **Laporan Perubahan Modal + Setoran/Prive** — new page `accounting/modal/page.tsx` ("📜 Perubahan Modal" in Akuntansi) with quick one-click "+ Setoran Modal"/"− Ambil Prive" forms (2-line manual journal against 1-001/3-001) plus a Statement-of-Changes-in-Equity report. Key design choice that avoids re-deriving pendapatan/beban per period (which would double-count if a Tutup Buku landed mid-period, see the Tutup Buku section above): compute Total Modal (`Modal Pemilik + Laba Ditahan + Laba Berjalan`, same 3-part sum Neraca uses) as of two snapshots — strictly before the period start, and as of the period end — then `Laba Bersih Periode Ini = (ModalAkhir − ModalAwal) − (Setoran − Prive)`, where Setoran/Prive come from summing credit/debit lines on the 3-001 account specifically within the period. This is mathematically exact regardless of whether a closing happened mid-period, without needing any closing-aware special-casing. Verified: Modal Akhir (period=all) matched Neraca's Total Modal exactly both before and after posting a real Rp1.000.000 setoran (which correctly flowed through to both pages identically and left "Rugi Bersih Periode Ini" unchanged, proving setoran/prive are cleanly separated from the profit figure).
- **Transfer Kas/Bank** — deliberately scoped down from "true multi-account Kas/Bank support" (which would require threading an account-selector through every auto-posting RPC: checkout, void, expenses, purchases, payroll, receivables — a much bigger change) to a lightweight manual-transfer shortcut at `accounting/transfer-kas/page.tsx` ("🔀 Transfer Kas/Bank" in Akuntansi): pick from/to accounts (any `type='aset'` account, so it picks up custom cash/bank accounts added via the pre-existing Daftar Akun "Tambah Akun Custom" feature) + amount, posts a 2-line entry. All automatic postings still hardcode `1-001`; the page's own copy says so explicitly. Verified: added a custom "1-002 Bank BCA" aset account via Daftar Akun, transferred Rp500.000 from Kas & Bank to it — Neraca showed both accounts adjust correctly (Kas & Bank −500rb, Bank BCA +500rb), Total Aset unchanged (pure internal transfer), balanced throughout.

**Tutup Buku (period closing) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-10**: new `public.period_closings` table (migration `20260710130000_period_closing.sql`, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) plus a `public.close_accounting_period(p_business_id, p_period_end)` RPC and a new `'tutup_buku'` value added to `journal_entries.source`'s check constraint. Mechanism: for every pendapatan/beban account with a nonzero all-time cumulative balance as of `p_period_end` (23:59:59+07 boundary, same convention as Neraca), the RPC posts one closing line that zeroes that account (debit a revenue account by its balance, credit an expense account by its balance), then one final line moving the net difference into `3-100 Laba Ditahan` (credit if profit, debit if loss) — built entirely from account balances computed server-side in plpgsql, passed to the existing `private.post_journal()` helper so it's guaranteed balanced. Key insight that kept this simple: because each closing zeroes the *all-time cumulative* balance (not a separate "since last close" window), no other report needed any code changes — Neraca's existing `totalPendapatan - totalBeban` query already naturally reflects only activity since the last closing, since prior activity nets to zero via the closing entry. RPC validates ownership, rejects future dates, and rejects closing at or before the last closing's `period_end` (enforces strictly increasing, no re-closing).
- New page `accounting/tutup-buku/page.tsx`: shows current unclosed Laba Berjalan (same calc as Neraca), last-closed date, a form to close as of a date (defaults to last day of previous month, confirm-step pattern like `MarkPaidButton`/`DeletePayslipButton`), and closing history. Neraca's footnote now links here and its wording changed from "belum punya proses tutup buku formal" to explain Laba Berjalan is "sejak tutup buku terakhir". Nav: "🔒 Tutup Buku" added to the Akuntansi sidebar group.
- Known limitation (accepted, in scope note): no hard lock preventing a backdated journal entry from landing before an already-closed `period_end` — would corrupt that period's zeroed balance. Not enforced across every posting action (purchases/finance/payroll/POS checkout) since that's a much bigger change; documented in the confirm-dialog copy as a "don't do this" convention instead, matching the existing "correct via reversing entry, not by editing old data" philosophy already used on the Jurnal page.
- Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": Laba Berjalan showed -Rp251.000 before closing. Closed as of 2026-07-10 → Tutup Buku page showed Laba Berjalan flip to Rp0 and the new entry in Riwayat Tutup Buku (-Rp251.000). Neraca confirmed: Laba Ditahan changed from Rp0 to -Rp251.000, Laba Berjalan (belum ditutup) now Rp0, Total Modal unchanged at -Rp251.000, Total Aset unchanged, "✓ Aset = Kewajiban + Modal (seimbang)" held throughout. Jurnal showed the actual closing entry: 4 balanced lines (Rp751.000 debit = Rp751.000 kredit) — credit Beban Gaji Rp700.000 and Beban Lain-lain Rp51.000 (zeroing both), debit Pendapatan Penjualan Rp500.000 (zeroing it), debit Laba Ditahan Rp251.000 (loss, so debited not credited) — confirming the sign logic for both profit and loss cases works (this test happened to be a loss; the profit-case credit branch is the same code path, not separately exercised but symmetric and low-risk).

Neraca confirmed balanced throughout (✓ Aset = Kewajiban + Modal), Piutang Usaha line correctly returned to Rp0 after full payment. **Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**
1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".
2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Fixed by extracting the calc into `src/lib/recalculate-product-cost.ts` (`recalculateProductCost` + a new `recalculateProductCostsForIngredient` that finds every product referencing a given ingredient and recalcs each) and calling the ingredient-scoped version from all three write sites whenever `unit_cost` actually changes. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": added Gula Pasir (50gr) to Roti Bakar's recipe (HPP → Rp1.350 at Rp27/gr), then edited Gula Pasir's price to Rp100/gr manually — Roti Bakar's HPP updated to Rp5.000 without touching the recipe. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.
3. **FIXED (commit e02e62d, migration `20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql`)**: `checkout_transaction` only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduced inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all. Fixed by decoupling the Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (posted only when `v_total > 0`) from the HPP/Persediaan lines (posted independently whenever `v_total_cost > 0`), building `v_journal_lines` incrementally and only calling `private.post_journal` if at least 2 lines ended up in it. Mirrored the identical fix in `void_transaction`'s reversing entry. Verified end-to-end in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Roti Bakar (HPP Rp5.300) with a 100% order discount (INV-20260709-0001, total Rp0) — jurnal correctly posted a 2-line entry (debit 5-001 HPP / credit 1-200 Persediaan, Rp5.300, no Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines). Then voided it with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly posted debit 1-200 / credit 5-001, Rp5.300. Neraca stayed balanced throughout.
4. **FIXED (commit 23c83ca)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` called the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }`. Now `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` return the error message (or null) instead of swallowing it, and both call sites plus the utang-payment RPC call in `addPurchasePayment` check it: on failure they log a `"warning"` activity entry (instead of the usual success level) with the error text, and return a form error telling the user the record saved but a manual correcting journal entry is needed at Akuntansi → Jurnal. Verified no regression on the happy path (a normal "Lain-lain" expense still saved silently with no error banner). The failure path itself wasn't exercised (would need deliberately breaking an account code) but the logic is a straightforward null-check/ternary, low risk.

**All 4 formula-audit bugs are now fixed** (commits bdbe337, b928d51, e02e62d, 23c83ca). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

**5th bug found and fixed 2026-07-10** (user asked "sebagai accounting & finance saran apa yg kurang" — a fresh accounting-lens review after the mini-ERP feature set was otherwise complete): `checkout_transaction` credited the **full transaction total — including PPN collected from the customer — straight to 4-001 Pendapatan Penjualan**. PPN isn't the business's revenue, it's a liability held on behalf of the tax office, so every taxed sale was overstating income with no corresponding "PPN payable" anywhere in Kewajiban. **Fixed migration `20260710140000_ppn_liability.sql`**: added `2-200 PPN Keluaran (Utang Pajak)` to the seeded COA (via `seed_default_accounts` + backfill for existing businesses), and redefined `checkout_transaction` to credit only `subtotal + service` to Pendapatan Penjualan while crediting `tax` to the new liability account instead (Kas & Bank debit for the full total is unchanged). `void_transaction`'s reversing entry mirrors the same split. Remitting the PPN later (paying the tax office) needs no new UI — the existing Jurnal Manual page already lists every account dynamically, so it's just a manual debit-2-200/credit-1-001 entry. Historical transactions posted before this fix keep their PPN baked into revenue (not retroactively corrected — would need a manual correcting entry if that matters).
- Verified E2E in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Kopi Susu (Rp18.000 + 5% layanan Rp900 + 10% PPN Rp1.890 = Rp20.790 total, tax_enabled/service_enabled both on for this business) → journal posted debit Kas & Bank 20.790 / credit Pendapatan Penjualan **18.900** (not 20.790) / credit PPN Keluaran **1.890**, plus the usual HPP/Persediaan lines, balanced (27.790 = 27.790 incl. HPP). Neraca showed PPN Keluaran Rp1.890 under Kewajiban and Laba Berjalan correctly reflecting only the Rp11.900 margin (18.900 revenue − 7.000 HPP), still balanced. Then voided the same transaction with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly flipped debit/credit on all three split lines (debit Pendapatan 18.900, debit PPN Keluaran 1.890, credit Kas & Bank 20.790, plus HPP/Persediaan reversal), balanced.

If PIN-pad or similar plain-onClick buttons ever seem unresponsive to `preview_click` again, switch to a JS `.click()` via `preview_eval` rather than assuming the credentials are wrong.

No migration needed — reads existing tables only.
- Verified in browser: right after the Tutup Buku test above, selecting "Semua" period showed **Rp0 everywhere** — correct, not a bug, since the closing entry (dated today, same as all the test activity) nets every pendapatan/beban account back to zero within any period range that includes it, exactly like a real closed period would. Sold 1 Roti Bakar afterward (new activity postdating the closing calc) — the report then correctly showed Pendapatan Penjualan Rp17.325 (subtotal+service only, no PPN — confirms the PPN fix above flows through here too), HPP Rp5.300, Laba Kotor Rp12.025, Laba Bersih Rp12.025, margin 69%, and this number matched Neraca's "Laba Berjalan (belum ditutup)" (also Rp12.025) exactly, confirming the two reports stay consistent with each other.

**Payroll auto-posting — built and verified E2E 2026-07-10**: the one payroll gap flagged in the 2026-07-09 formula audit ("Payroll does NOT auto-post yet") is now closed. Migration `20260710100000_payslip_paid.sql` adds `payslips.paid_at timestamptz` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]). New action `markPayslipPaid` in `payroll/actions.ts` sums `base_pay + tunjangan − potongan` from `payslip_adjustments`, sets `paid_at`, and posts a journal entry via the same `post_journal_entry` RPC pattern as expenses/purchases (debit `5-100` Beban Gaji, credit `1-001` Kas & Bank) — same fire-and-report error handling (journal failure doesn't roll back the payslip, just logs a warning activity entry and returns a correction-needed message). Once paid, a payslip is locked: `addPayslipAdjustment`, `deletePayslipAdjustment`, and `deletePayslip` all now check `paid_at` and refuse to mutate/delete (returning a friendly error) since the journal entry already reflects the old total. New `MarkPaidButton` client component (confirm-step pattern like `DeletePayslipButton`) on the payslip detail page; once paid, the tunjangan/potongan form is replaced with a "sudah dibayar" notice and per-line delete buttons disappear. List page shows a "✓ Dibayar" badge. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": created a payslip for Manajer Test (Rp0 base pay, no attendance), added a Rp150.000 "Bonus Test" tunjangan, marked paid → Jurnal correctly showed debit Beban Gaji / credit Kas & Bank Rp150.000, Neraca stayed balanced. Confirmed delete guard: attempting to delete the paid payslip showed "Slip gaji yang sudah dibayar tidak bisa dihapus (sudah ada di jurnal)" instead of deleting.
- Payroll's accounting picture is now complete: sales, expenses, purchases, and payroll all auto-post; only Akuntansi's own manual-entry pages don't need auto-posting since they *are* the manual path.

**THR/Lembur first-class fields — built and verified E2E 2026-07-10**: closes the last gap noted above. User chose manual-nominal-only for both (no jam×tarif breakdown for lembur, no proportional-tenure formula for THR — both vary too much per business to hardcode). Migration `20260710110000_payslip_thr_lembur.sql` adds `payslips.lembur_amount`/`thr_amount numeric not null default 0`. New action `updatePayslipExtras` (payroll/actions.ts) updates both at once, guarded by the same `paid_at` lock as adjustments. New `LemburThrForm` client component (payroll/[payslipId]/lembur-thr-form.tsx) — two number inputs + one save button, edits both fields together rather than one-at-a-time like the generic adjustment list. Both the payslip detail breakdown and the payroll list's total now fold `lembur_amount + thr_amount` into `totalDiterima`/`total`, and `markPayslipPaid`'s journal-posting total includes them too. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": created a payslip for Manajer Test (Rp0 base pay), set Lembur Rp200.000 + THR Rp350.000 via the new form, breakdown showed both lines and Total Diterima Rp550.000, marked paid → jurnal posted debit Beban Gaji/credit Kas & Bank Rp550.000 (not just base pay), Neraca stayed balanced (✓ Aset = Kewajiban + Modal).

**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). Same owner account also has a ticket-venue business "Kolam Renang Test" (id `f43c8529-7fe5-4074-9e98-43335da31267`, 🎟️ Tempat Wisata/Tiket) with cashier "Kasir Tiket" (role manajer) — PIN reset to `1234` on 2026-07-07 via Kelola Kasir (original PIN unknown), an open shift, ticket categories Pengunjung/Rp25.000/Penunggu/Rp10.000/Yoga clas/Rp340.000, and members "Budi Member" (M-0001) plus test-added "Budi Tester" (MBR-001, member_price Rp0 for Pengunjung). Confirmed working end-to-end: manual physical ticket numbers on checkout (duplicate number correctly rejected with a friendly error), member lookup/pricing in POS, ticket-reports reconciliation list, CSV export (`/ticket-reports/export?type=transactions&period=today`), member barcode card (`/members/<id>/card`, uses jsbarcode), and transaction detail/void page.

**Why:** the real owner's password is unknown, and the proxy redirects all /business routes to /login, so preview verification needs its own account.

**How to apply:** log in at /login with these credentials, then navigate to /business/<id>/... pages. Note: Turbopack on the slow G: drive sometimes serves stale CSS after globals.css edits — `rm -rf .next` and restart the dev server if new Tailwind utilities don't apply. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]]. The POS PIN keypad (pin-screen.tsx) is plain React state, not a real input — driving it with `preview_eval` by firing all 4 digit clicks in one synchronous block silently fails (React batches the clicks and reads a stale `pin` closure each time, so it never reaches length 4 and neither succeeds nor shows an error). Use separate calls per digit, one per tool call, so each click gets its own render cycle. **Update 2026-07-10**: even one-at-a-time, the `preview_click` *tool* (as opposed to `preview_eval`) reliably failed to register on these digit buttons at all — no server action ever fired (confirmed via server logs showing zero `verifyPin` calls), tried across a fresh page load, multiple reloads, and 1-3s waits between clicks. Switching each digit press to `preview_eval` with `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.grid.grid-cols-3.gap-3 button')).find(b => b.textContent.trim() === '<digit>').click()` worked on the very first attempt. If `preview_click` ever seems unresponsive on this keypad (or similar plain-onClick grids) again, don't assume the PIN/credentials are wrong — switch to the `preview_eval` `.click()` approach first.
